new_statements.rule_in_words: Nyokon is described as a terraced-level tone language (H, L, downstep/downdrift; contour tones on long vowels and sonorant codas). Neither primary phonological description (Lovestrand 2011, 42 pp; Mous 2022) makes any statement about word stress or accent; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None (no stress statement). Prosodic remarks only: phrase-final devoicing of all segments including vowels; closed syllables almost only word-final; V syllables only word-initial (prefixes).
new_statements.domain_note: Lovestrand's data are isolated wordlist citation forms (SILCAWL 1700 list); Mous's are elicited sentences and texts. Tone is lexical and grammatical (TAM marked tonally).
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe Nyokon [nvo] = nyok1243 itself (villages Nyokon and Makénéné, Mbam, Centre Region). Lovestrand 2011 is based on wordlists from Nyokon-village speakers; Mous 2022 on one speaker (Viviane Kigno Abwa-Yah) whose speech differs slightly (glottal stop for Lovestrand's voiced pharyngeal fricative). JWAL's web slug misspells the title as 'Nyakon'; the article itself is 'Nyokon'. Not to be confused with Tunen/Nen (A.44, tune1261), of which Ethnologue formerly listed Nyokon as a dialect.
